correctness.rationale: The vertex-coordinate bracket is exactly AB with A=(u,u') and B=(w';-w), a bijective reparameterization of ordered vertex pairs, including in characteristic two; the two free central inputs supply q^{2ab}. For a fixed rank-r target, count A of rank s by first choosing an s-plane containing the target image, then a surjection from k² onto it. For each such A every target column has q^{2-s} preimages. The resulting normalized count is the sum over r<=s<=2 of [a-r choose s-r]_q times the product of (q²-q^i) for 0<=i<s, times q^{(2-s)b}. Expanding gives exactly the three displayed nonempty counts, the symmetry at zero, and empty fibers above rank two. The image consists of matrices of rank at most two over every field; the derived ideal is all central matrices since edge basis elements are individual brackets. Rank subadditivity bounds the number of brackets below by ceil(r/2); a decomposition into r rank-one matrices grouped two at a time attains it, with zero requiring none. Full-rank targets give the stated width. Choosing image and quotient bases gives the ordinary rank census and hence the normalization; the rank-two stratum has dimension 2(a+b-2), yielding the stated codimension when both parts have size at least three. An independent weighted-convolution replay and separate rank tests checked every target and rank count at (a,b,q)=(4,4,2),(2,2,5). The normalized nonempty fibers were (1186,90,6) and (4705,1080,480); ranks 3 and 4 were absent from the first image. The factor for central inputs and the arbitrary-field width rest on the proof, not on enumeration.
residual_risks: The independent replay is bounded to those dimensions and prime fields; field generality follows from the counting and rank arguments.

evidence: Writing lambda=q^a+q^b-1 for the zero outer-product weight, the normalized bracket fibers at ranks 0,1,2 are respectively lambda²+(q-1)² b0, 2 lambda(q-1)+(q-1)² a1, and (q-1)² c2. The counts vanish above two. Negating the second outer product does not change any weight. Algebraic expansion recovers the frozen formulas exactly.

A rank-two-or-less step is exactly a step of length at most two in rank-one distance, over any field. The minimum number of such steps is ceil(rank/2), with zero at distance zero; rank reaches min(a,b).

The additional arbitrary-field wording uses a rank argument that does not depend on finiteness; the threshold, width and image are direct consequences of grouping rank-one summands. originality.rationale: The full finite-field census is mechanically implied by the classical bilinear-forms graph intersection array, explicitly confirmed in the general-q statement of Gavrilyuk–Koolen, arXiv:1511.09435v2, §2.4, equations (5)–(6) and Result 2.2. A bracket is an ordered sum of two rank-one or zero matrices; each nonzero rank-one summand has q-1 input factorizations and zero has q^a+q^b-1. The fixed-target convolution is therefore a fixed scalar combination of the known intersection numbers, plus a free central factor. Width is rank-metric distance in the square of the rank-one-difference graph; over an arbitrary field the same formula is an immediate rank-decomposition consequence. Using the graphical Lie-algebra name does not change the underlying census or produce an independent new boundary. No claim is made that the older paper explicitly stated the Lie-algebra wording.
residual_risks: The exact historical priority of the graphical Lie wording was not resolved. The primary Delsarte and Dani–Mainkar bodies remained inaccessible; the originality failure rests on the positively verified implication from the open general-q array, not on these access failures.

value.rationale: The natural exact invariant is correctly explained, but its formula is a weighted two-step count in a classical distance-regular graph, the image and width are immediate rank consequences, and the remaining normalization and codimension are standard determinantal counts. There is no new invariant or nonmechanically implied boundary beyond that change of presentation. This can be useful exposition but is not a separate valuable research finding under the stated standard.
residual_risks: The assessment is limited to full bicliques; no deduction is made about arbitrary graphical Lie algebras or the value of a different new graph family.
